body.x: IDCITI Co., Ltd. (CEO Jihoon Ryoo) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

IDCITI is a pioneer in providing precise indoor positioning solutions. Its innovative uGPS (underground GPS) technology is designed to address the challenges of GPS signal blackouts in shadowed areas.

A company representative explained, "Indoor positioning information is crucial in various scenarios, including traffic information systems, large facility operations, and emergencies. However, GPS signals are unavailable in underground or indoor environments. GPS, a proprietary technology of IDCITI, is significantly more robust than traditional GPS repeaters and delivers uninterrupted signals in real-time, even to fast-moving vehicles and indoor or underground locations."
The uGPS system is tailored to the needs of diverse industries and offers a fundamental solution to indoor positioning challenges.

At CES 2025, IDCITI highlighted the unique advantages of its technology, capturing the attention of global visitors. The company emphasized the versatility and scalability of its satellite software system. Users can employ the solution with existing GPS receivers without requiring additional hardware or software installations. The system is suitable for worldwide applications and is built on global standard GNSS technology.

body.cap: uGPS system diagram | Image by IDCITI

body.x: The uGPS system also supports vehicles traveling at high speeds (up to 100 km/h), ensuring seamless GNSS signals between indoor and outdoor environments. It offers superior price competitiveness at just one-tenth the cost of overseas products. Additionally, it requires no preprocessing, is operational immediately after installation, and features low maintenance costs, enhancing user convenience.

IDCITI has already demonstrated its expertise in the "Technology Development and Verification Study to Resolve Satellite Positioning Blackouts on Highways" in 2023. The company installed its uGPS system in sections of the Seoul Ring Expressway, including the 1.8 km and 1.2 km segments of the Suri-Suam Tunnel (Ilsan-bound).

IDCITI's achievements include resolving satellite signal limitations in the uphill section of Namsan Tunnel 1, providing GPS services in the underground parking lot of Incheon Startup Park, and reducing bus arrival time errors at the Jamsil Bus Transfer Center from 600 seconds to just 14 seconds.
